festivals: Kalpathy Ratholsavam - 10-day annual chariot festival in Thulam (November); Maha Shivaratri

history.period: Early 15th century (1424-25 AD per inscription; 1464 AD per Sewell's list - conflict flagged)
history.summary: Oldest Siva temple of Malabar, on the southern bank of the Kalpathy (Nila Bhagirathi) river, founded around 1425 AD by Ittikombi Achan (Kombi Achan), the then Raja of Palakkad, under the patronage of the Palakkad royal family. Legend holds that a Brahmin widow, Lakshmiammal, returned from Kashi with a lingam and installed it here on the river bank, modelling the shrine on the Kashi Vishwanath temple on the Ganges - hence the moniker 'Kasiyil Pakuthi Kalpathy' (Half Kashi) or Dakshina Kashi. A kolezhuthu stone inscription in the courtyard records an endowment by Ittikombi Achan in Malayalam Era 600 (1424-25 AD), implying the temple predates it, while Sewell's list and Logan's Malabar Manual give consecration/endowment in Kollam year 640 (1464 AD) - a date conflict. The temple is the centre of the Kalpathy agraharam, the first heritage village of Kerala and one of the earliest Tamil Brahmin settlements in the state; four agraharams (New Kalpathy, Old Kalpathy, Chathapuram, Govindarajapuram) ring the shrine. The Ratholsavam chariot festival, as old as the temple, entered the state government's festival list in 1986. name: Kalpathy Viswanatha Swamy Temple
town_description: Kalpathy is a historic Tamil Brahmin agraharam quarter in Palakkad city, Kerala - the state's first heritage village. Lined with traditional houses leading to its temples, it is known as a hub of Carnatic music and Vedic learning, and hosts the famous annual Ratholsavam.
